results.reason: I found no failed condition. (1) Figures verified against the sources. P-955 p.9: consensus-LCA 'concordant diagnoses for 90% of cases', N = 354 (p.4), consensus NC or MCI only. P-1084 Table 2 (p.7): NC column oCN 3081, tCN 5797, aMCI 3937, mMCI-Mild 2354, mMCI-Severe 836 (total 16,005); MCI column 232, 1115, 2283, 2586, 2297 (total 8,513). Restricted to NC and MCI to match P-955's frame: concordant = 3081 + 5797 + 2283 + 2586 + 2297 = 16,044 of 24,518 = 0.654 (Wilson about 0.648-0.660). Kappa: p_e = (16005 x 10225 + 8513 x 14293)/24518^2 = 285,327,434/601,132,324 = 0.4747, kappa = (0.6544 - 0.4747)/0.5253 = 0.342. The P-955 Wilson interval for 0.90 at n = 354 is 0.864-0.927. Each estimate lies far outside the other's interval. (2) Matched-figure hunt. P-1084 prints no analysis with published norms, with LCA, within one ADRC, or with an agreement statistic of its own. Its NC-only cluster analysis (p.7) answers a different question. P-955 prints no robust-CN analysis. P-955's two nearest variants both leave the gap: race-adjusted norms (consensus-LCA kappa 0.79 against 0.80) and the Jak/Bondi actuarial rule (100 - 13 - 3 = 84% concordance, Wilson about 0.798-0.875). (3) Condition 1 holds. Both papers compare data-driven neuropsychological classification with consensus MCI/NC in ADRC participants, and P-1084 itself calls its result different from P-955's (p.11). (4) No explanation is shown to be sufficient. P-1084 shows that NACC consensus tracks CDR (about 90% of NC at CDR 0 and of MCI at CDR 0.5 or above), but it shows no comparison with how Penn's consensus was made. I add one explanation the reader did not list: P-955's consensus itself used 'comprehensive neuropsychological data', whereas NACC diagnoses may come from a single physician. Caveat, not a condition: Penn ADRC contributes to NACC (grant P30 AG072979 in P-1084's acknowledgments), so the data partly overlap.

figures.P-955: Consensus against LCA, N = 354: concordance 90% (printed), Wilson 0.864-0.927; kappa 0.80 (race-adjusted 0.79). LCA MCI 41% against consensus 44%. Actuarial against consensus: 84% (13% + 3% discordant), Wilson about 0.798-0.875, kappa 0.68.
figures.P-1084: Table 2 restricted to consensus NC (16,005) and MCI (8,513): concordance 16,044/24,518 = 0.654 (Wilson about 0.648-0.660); kappa 0.342; cluster MCI 14,293/24,518 = 58.3% against consensus MCI 34.7%. Printed for the whole sample: cluster MCI 58.8% against consensus 32.4% plus 6.6% impaired-not-MCI.

candidate_explanations: Normative reference: robust-CN regression norms in P-1084 against published age/education/sex norms in P-955 (P-1084 p.11: 'only the current study derived z scores from the performance of robust cognitively normal participants'; 'Robust norms may create a higher standard for normal'). Untested in both papers.

Sampling frame: one ADRC with 44% consensus MCI against 46 NACC ADRCs with 32.4% (P-1084 p.11: 'the previous study was conducted in a sample of participants from one ADRC while we used the larger NACC UDS sample').

How the reference label is made: P-955's consensus used 'comprehensive neuropsychological data' (p.5), the same test information LCA uses. NACC consensus is 'heavily driven by CDR scores' (P-1084 p.7), and at some sites 'diagnosis is made by either a consensus team or a single physician' (P-1084 p.3).
Impairment threshold implied by the cluster-MCI groups (1 SD below the mean on several scores) against P-955's consensus rule of 'an impaired score ... on at least one cognitive test' (P-955 p.5).
Algorithm and input representation: 5-class LCA on six domain means (P-955 p.5) against Ward hierarchical clustering on individual test z-scores (P-1084 p.3).
Battery: 14 measures in 6 domains including CERAD list learning, recall and praxis (P-955) against a UDS subset of memory, span, TMT, category fluency and naming (P-1084).

results.reason: I found no failed condition. (1) Counts verified. P-986 Table 2 (p.9): Petersen standard 323/744 = 43.4% (39.8-47.0); relaxed follow-up 448/1063 = 42.1%; impairment-only 684/1579 = 43.3%. NP standard 181/375 = 48.3% (43.2-53.5); relaxed 239/528 = 45.3%; impairment-only 350/773 = 45.3%; original NP without complaint 289/528 = 54.7% (50.4-59.0). Same participants, n = 334 (p.6): 32.9% against 46.4%. P-1136 p.4: consistency 177 (63.2%) against 121 (43.2%) of 280, McNemar 32.9. P-1136 Table 3 (p.5): conventional reverters 192, consistent 133; NP reverters 246, consistent 285; incident dementia among reverters 20 and 9, among consistent 43 and 73. (2) Arithmetic re-done. P-986 Petersen minus NP = -0.049, SE sqrt(.434x.566/744 + .483x.517/375) = 0.0316, CI -0.111 to +0.013. P-1136 Table 3: 192/325 = 0.591 against 246/531 = 0.463, difference +0.128, SE 0.0348, CI +0.060 to +0.196. McNemar with continuity correction: (56 - 1)^2/(b + c) = 32.9 gives b + c = 92. Paired SE = sqrt(92 - 56^2/280)/280 = 0.0321, so +0.200 (0.137-0.263). The primary intervals (-0.111 to +0.013 against +0.060 to +0.196) do not overlap. The same-participant analyses are significant in opposite directions: -0.135 (about -0.209 to -0.062) against +0.200 (0.137-0.263). (3) Matched figures all keep the gap. On the NP rule, P-986's original Jak/Bondi version (P-1136's rule) widens it. On consistency, P-1136 counts anyone still meeting 'criteria for cognitive impairment' as consistent, so losing a complaint may not break consistency. P-986's variant (a), with no complaint or ADL requirement at follow-up, is the matching case: -0.031 (-0.083 to +0.021), which does not overlap P-1136's intervals. For progressors, removing incident dementia from P-1136's counts gives 172/262 = 0.656 against 237/449 = 0.528, +0.129 (about 0.055-0.202). (4) Condition 1 holds: community population cohorts, algorithmic neuropsychological criteria, and P-1136 p.7 itself names 'contrasting results' against Overton et al. (P-986). Neither paper shows any explanation to be sufficient.

Relaxed follow-up -0.031 (-0.083 to +0.021); impairment-only -0.020 (-0.062 to +0.023); against original NP 54.7%, -0.113 (-0.169 to -0.058); same participants (n = 334) 32.9% against 46.4%, -0.135 (-0.209 to -0.062, independence SE; a paired SE would be narrower).

Table 3 full sample: 59.1% against 46.3%, +0.128 (0.060-0.196). Progressors removed: 65.6% against 52.8%, +0.129 (0.055-0.202).

candidate_explanations: Age window and cohort: InveCe.Ab enrolled one birth cohort aged 70-74 at baseline (P-1136 p.2); GAS/SNAC pooled random samples aged 60 and over, with a mean age of 68 at first MCI (P-986 p.6).
Subjective-complaint prevalence, which the conventional rule requires: 'probably lower than that in the clinical setting' in P-1136 (p.7), making conventional MCI rarer (18.5% against 43.8% NP).
Education: low and heterogeneous in InveCe.Ab, mean 7.2 years (P-1136 p.2).

Stability definition: P-1136 counts as consistent anyone who keeps 'fulfilling the criteria for cognitive impairment in subsequent waves (regardless of dementia diagnosis)' (p.10). P-986 requires reverters to keep complaint and ADL, and excludes progressors (p.4). Both parts were approximately tested, and the gap stays.

Same-participant frame: P-986's n = 334 are participants with 'enough data to fulfil both criteria, and ... complete follow-up data' (p.5), not necessarily MCI under both. P-1136's 280 had MCI under both criteria.
Follow-up cadence: every 3 or 6 years depending on age (P-986) against waves at 0, 2, 4, 8 and 12 years with up to four follow-ups (P-1136).
Norms and cut-offs: external SNAC-Blekinge/Stockholm 7th/16th percentile norms (P-986 p.4) against internal InveCe.Ab normative samples (P-1136).

results.reason: I found no failed condition, though the comparator difference is large. (1) The misread-figure risk is closed. I extracted P-1157's Figure 3 image from the PDF (p.7) and read it directly. The 15 categories are Antihypertensive Drugs, Antipsychotic/Anxiolytic, Antithrombotic, Lipid-modifying, Supplements, Antidiabetic, Ergot Alkaloid Derivatives, Urologic, Hypnotics, Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, Laxatives, Antidepressants, Acid-Related, Cardiac Vasodilators and Antihistamines. There is no separate CCB, RAS, beta-blocker or diuretic category, so 'Antihypertensive Drugs' is the pooled class, not ATC C02 alone. P-999's pooled contrast is therefore the right match: any AHM against no AHM. The HR 0.59 (0.37-0.93) is printed in P-1157's text (p.5), and the plotted point (about 0.56, CI about 0.34-0.92) agrees. P-999 Table 3 (p.13) prints any AHM 1.06 (1.04-1.08), P < 0.001. (2) Condition 4: the two estimates are significant in opposite directions and their intervals do not overlap. (3) Matched figure: none. P-1157 prints no AHM estimate among its 154 hypertensive participants and no co-medication-adjusted model; its covariates include neither hypertension nor any drug. P-999 prints nothing that includes normotensives or uses baseline-only exposure. The statin-user stratum, 0.84 (0.80-0.88), does overlap P-1157's interval, but P-1157 is not a statin-user population, so it is not a matched figure. (4) Condition 1 is the strongest challenge. P-1157's unexposed group is mostly normotensive, whereas P-999's non-users are all untreated hypertensives. P-999 itself warns that in a mixed population AHM use is confounded by hypertension status. P-1157's own counts make this concrete: progression was 47/154 = 30.5% among hypertensives against 42/83 = 50.6% among normotensives, a crude ratio of 0.60, nearly the AHM HR of 0.59. That supports the explanation but does not show it is sufficient, since no within-hypertensive AHM estimate is printed. The named factor, outcome and channel are the same. P-1157 frames its estimate as the treatment question P-999 asks (p.7: 'Consistent with prior studies, we observed that antihypertensive treatment was significantly associated with a reduced risk of dementia'), so the difference counts as an allowed population restriction and the lead candidate explanation.

figures.P-999: Any AHM users against non-users, hypertensive MCI, N = 128,683 (100,678 against 28,005), incident claims ADRD: aHR 1.06 (1.04-1.08), printed in Table 3 and on p.14. Strata: with statins 0.84 (0.80-0.88), without 1.11 (1.08-1.13); with metformin 0.86 (0.76-0.96), without 1.06 (1.04-1.08). Per class against non-users of that class: 0.96-0.98.
figures.P-1157: Baseline antihypertensive drugs (pooled category, Figure 3) against none, CDR 0.5 to CDR 1, N = 237 (89 progressed): HR 0.59 (0.37-0.93), printed on p.5. Crude, from Table 1 hypertension counts (107/148 non-progressors, 47/89 progressors): progression 30.5% in hypertensives against 50.6% in normotensives, ratio 0.60.

candidate_explanations: Population and reference group: P-999 is restricted to hypertensive MCI, so its comparator is untreated hypertensives. P-1157's unexposed group is mostly normotensive, and its models include no hypertension term. P-999 p.9: 'including normotensive patients with MCI to our population would add a potential confounder (hypertension status) that could not be well controlled as very few normotensive patients are taking AHMs.' In P-1157 hypertension is more common in non-progressors (72.3% against 52.8%, p = 0.003), and the crude hypertension ratio (0.60) nearly equals the AHM HR (0.59).

Co-medication: P-999 adjusts for statin and metformin, and its AHM estimate reverses with statin co-use (0.84 against 1.11; p.17). P-1157's per-category models adjust for no medication, and lipid-modifying agents are separately protective (0.43).
Exposure window: baseline prescription records (P-1157 p.4) against consumption 'during the study period' (P-999 p.4).

Outcome ascertainment: claims ICD codes including non-specific codes such as R41.81, or two anti-dementia fills within 6 months, with 55.6% incidence (71,558/128,683; P-999 pp.8, 13). P-1157 uses neurologist-confirmed CDR 0.5 to 1. P-999's printed code lists put G31.83 in both the MCI and the dementia definitions, and COPD codes under hypertension (evident transcription errors in a preprint).
Setting and size: US Optum commercial claims (N = 128,683) against Taiwanese veterans, institutionalised and outpatient (N = 237).
Multiplicity: P-1157's estimate is one of 15 exploratory per-category Cox models tested at p < 0.05 without correction (p.4).

results.reason: No condition fails on the source texts, but this is the thinnest of the four. (1) Figures verified. P-680 p.5: aerobic 1.442, Z 3.456, so SE = 0.417 and the CI is 0.624-2.260; the Results' 0.642 is a typo, and the Abstract (p.1) and Discussion (p.14) print 0.624. P-683 Table 2 (p.6): AEwtM global cognition g 0.48 (0.18-0.79), SE about 0.156. Two-sample z = 0.962/sqrt(0.417^2 + 0.156^2) = 2.16. (2) Condition 4: each point estimate lies outside the other's interval, which is the rule's first test and the test other readers applied to SMD pairs this round (C-243). The intervals do overlap between 0.624 and 0.79. If the association clause ('intervals that do not overlap') were applied to intervention SMDs, the pair would fail. I do not apply it, because an exercise-against-control SMD is an intervention effect, not a factor association, but I flag the point. (3) Matched figures. P-680's aerobic class spans P-683's three nodes: AEwtM (Amjad, Varela), AEwM (Song & Yu) and dance (Qi 2018/2019, same DOI). So P-683's all-type multivariate global-cognition estimate, 0.53 (0.16-0.90, Appendix E, rho = 0.6), is the closest class match. 1.442 lies outside it, and 0.53 lies outside 0.624-2.260 (z = 0.912/sqrt(0.417^2 + 0.189^2) = 1.99). My inverse-variance combination of P-683's three node estimates (0.48, 1.2, 0.55) gives about 0.58 (0.34-0.81), also outside. The quality-restricted AEwtM, 0.6 (0.28-0.93, Appendix L), is only a partial match: P-683 drops high RoB2 risk, while P-680 dropped two Downs and Black 'poor' studies. 1.442 lies outside its interval, and 0.6 misses 0.624 by 0.024. A formal two-sample test there gives z = 1.88, below 1.96, so the gap on that variant is within uncertainty by a two-sample test though beyond it by the brief's interval rule. (4) Condition 1 holds: both ask how much aerobic exercise against control improves cognition in older adults with MCI. One difference the reader missed: P-683's controls include balance/stretching/toning (7 trials), a home exercise programme and low-intensity non-aerobic exercise (p.5-6), whereas P-680 excluded studies without a no-exercise condition (p.3). This is a candidate explanation, not a change of question. The record's biomarker-subset story is unsupported, but the compared figures are printed values.

figures.P-680: Aerobic against no-exercise control, composite of all cognitive tests per study, amnestic trials excluded, 5 studies / 6 comparisons: SMD 1.442 (0.624-2.260; SE 0.417 from Z 3.456; I2 88.9%; prediction interval -1.440 to 4.324). All exercise: 1.165 (0.741-1.589).
figures.P-683: Global cognition, change-score Hedges g: AEwtM 0.48 (0.18-0.79; 26 effect sizes, 11 trials, n = 683); AEwM 1.2 (0.47-1.94); dance 0.55 (0.13-0.96); AEwtM with high risk of bias excluded 0.6 (0.28-0.93); multivariate all types 0.53 (0.16-0.90) at rho = 0.6 (0.51-0.55 across rho 0.2-0.8).

candidate_explanations: Intervention class: P-680's 'aerobic' includes Song & Yu 2019 (P-683: aerobic with music, g 1.2) and Qi 2019 (P-683: dance, as Qi 2018, DOI 10.3892/etm.2018.7006), and Bademli 2019, which P-683 excluded (P-680 p.14; P-683 p.5).

Comparator: P-680 required a no-exercise condition (p.3). P-683's controls include balance/stretching/toning (N = 7), a home exercise programme and low-intensity non-aerobic exercise alongside usual care and education (pp.5-6), which could shrink its effects.

Outcome construct: a per-study composite across all domains (P-680 p.15) against the global-cognition domain (P-683). P-683's AEwtM effects in other domains are smaller (executive 0.05, processing speed 0.29), so this runs against explaining P-680's larger value.
Population: amnestic MCI left out of P-680's analysis (p.5); P-683's AEwtM node includes amnestic trials (Tarumi 2019, Stuckenschneider 2021).
Design: P-680 admits non-randomised controlled studies (Downs and Black checklist); P-683 admits RCTs only.
Evidence base and heterogeneity: 5 studies with I2 about 89% and a prediction interval of -1.440 to 4.324 (P-680) against 11 trials in a multilevel model (P-683).
Change-SD standardisation: P-683 imputes missing change SDs with r = 0.68 (p.4); P-680 uses study pre-post correlations, value not stated.
